F-R shared-input: the slope-row mass X = sum_r m(r)^2 = E_Q(h) = sum_{kappa in Q minus {1}} c_h(kappa)^2 for the actual mu, h(z)=g(1-z), counting norms, hypotheses (H1),(H2),(H4) of Round 182. F's rich-fibre criterion (RF) at tau=p^(1/1280) is equivalent to X=O(p^(1+1/1280)) because light fibres contribute at most tau M_1 = O(p^(1+1/1280)) (F Proposition B, audit correction (a2)); within the admissible coset family g_H (F Proposition C, w worth exactly 3/4) a bound on X is also necessary for (H1)/(H2)/(H4)-only arguments. R's candidate shared lemma (SL) is X=O(p^(1+epsilon)), entering as W_xi <= X in the Round 178 point-plane bound for E(mu); any epsilon<3/16 improves the one-match exponent 115/64, and R needs only the weaker max_xi W_xi = O(p^(1+epsilon)). F's scale (epsilon <= 1/1280) implies R's; R's scale gives F only M_w=O(p^(1+epsilon)), an improvement on 11/8 but not the target. Both use the accepted Round 182 value X <= E^x(h) = O(p^(34/23)). sum g^2 is a shared hypothesis at different scales, not a shared estimate. No lemma was proved twice. Coordinator classification against the pre-dispatch record: that record (comparison_status assessed, known_shared []) stated affirmatively that the two ordinary calls share the object mu but no estimate, and named only sum g^2 as a possible shared input. The shared estimate X is therefore recorded as a missed group. The identification of (RF) with X and R's use of X as an upper bound for W_xi are both Round 183 outputs, so the miss was not visible from the Round 182 sources; the auditor judged that knowing it would not have changed the Round 183 calls.
